questions.prompt: What is the fundamental cause of an RxJS memory leak?

options.text: A subscription to a source that never completes, which is never unsubscribed
Using too many operators in a pipe
Calling map more than once
Subscribing to a completing HTTP request

questions.explanation: Infinite sources (interval, fromEvent, WebSockets) that are never unsubscribed keep their resources alive forever. Completing sources tear themselves down.

questions.prompt: Do you need to manually unsubscribe from a stream that completes, such as a single HTTP request?

options.text: No — a completing stream tears itself down automatically
Yes — every subscription must be manually unsubscribed
Only if it used map
Only in TypeScript

questions.explanation: When a stream completes (or errors), it runs teardown automatically. Manual unsubscription discipline is only required for infinite streams.

questions.prompt: What is the fix for a nested subscribe like `outer$.subscribe(x => inner$(x).subscribe(use))`?

options.text: Flatten it with a *Map operator, e.g. outer$.pipe(switchMap(x => inner$(x)))
Add a second Subject
Wrap both subscribes in setTimeout
Call unsubscribe twice

questions.explanation: Nested subscribes lose cancellation/error handling and leak inner subscriptions. A flattening operator (switchMap/mergeMap/concatMap) manages the inner subscriptions properly.

questions.prompt: In the `takeUntil(destroy$)` pattern, where should `takeUntil` be placed?

options.text: Last in the pipe, so it governs the whole chain's teardown
First, before any other operator
Immediately after the source only
It can go anywhere with no effect

questions.explanation: Placing takeUntil last ensures operators like mergeMap/combineLatest don't keep inner subscriptions alive past the destroy signal.

questions.prompt: Side effects belong in this operator, not in map/filter callbacks. Type the operator name.
questions.explanation: tap is for side effects (logging, analytics, DOM writes). Keeping map/filter pure makes pipelines testable and predictable.

questions.prompt: Which are valid strategies for managing subscription lifetime? Select all that apply.

options.text: Auto-completing operators like take(1), first(), takeWhile
takeUntil(destroy$) fired on teardown
Letting the framework subscribe/unsubscribe (e.g., Angular async pipe)
Ignoring cleanup because the garbage collector handles active subscriptions

questions.explanation: Bounded auto-completion, takeUntil, and framework-managed binding are all sound. The GC cannot reclaim an active subscription that still holds references — you must complete or unsubscribe it.
